cards: David was, according to the Hebrew Bible, the second king of the united kingdom of Israel and Judah, successor of Saul and father of Solomon, who made Jerusalem his capital.
Shoshenq I was a chief of the Libyan Meshwesh who became pharaoh around 943 BCE and founded the Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt, succeeding Psusennes II peacefully.
r. c. 943–922 BCE · Ancient Near East
Rehoboam was the son of Solomon and, according to the Hebrew Bible, the first king of Judah after the division of the united monarchy around 930 BCE.
Jeroboam I was the first king of the northern Kingdom of Israel, reigning from about 931 to 910 BCE according to the Hebrew Bible.
King Zhao of Zhou was the fourth king of the Western Zhou dynasty, reigning in the late tenth century BCE.
Nabu-mukin-apli was king of Babylon from about 978 to 943 BCE and the first ruler of the Dynasty of E.
r. c. 978–943 BCE · Ancient Near East
Osorkon the Elder was a king of the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt in the late 10th century BCE, ruling from Tanis for about six years.
Psusennes II was the last king of the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt, reigning in the mid-10th century BCE.
Siamun was a king of the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from Tanis for about nineteen years in the 10th century BCE.
Nadab was king of Israel in the late tenth century BCE, the son and successor of Jeroboam I.
